title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Iran: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Iran: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Iran: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: Managing post-death legal and administrative steps in Iran requires coordinating local medical, civil-registry, judicial, and tax authorities under a civil-law system grounded in Islamic jurisprudence [1][4]. Because several domestic Iranian portals (including the Legal Medicine Organization, Ministry of Health, parliamentary statutory databases, and certain Social Security Organization document endpoints) block external HTTPS requests from abroad or lack English administrative workflows, this guide combines reachable domestic authorities such as the National Organization for Civil Registration (Sabte Ahval) with verified international legal repositories (WIPO Lex, FAOLEX, and ILO NATLEX) and official foreign consular and civil-document reciprocity pages, advising direct verification in person or through a formally authorized representative in Iran [1][2][3][6][9].

steps.title: Medical release, post-mortem rules, and mortuary handling
steps.html:
• Hospital vs. out-of-hospital deaths: When a death occurs outside a hospital, local police refer the case for forensic examination, and release of the body requires authorization from the Prosecutor's Office; if cause of death is under investigation, test and forensic reports can take up to three months to finalize [1].
  • Autopsy and Tehran Legal Medicine Organization rules: Under Islamic law, burial takes place promptly and routine autopsies are uncommon unless the death appears unnatural or suspicious, in which case authorities may order a post-mortem without family consent; provincial hospitals provide short-term cold storage, whereas embalming and official autopsy halls for international cases are centralized at the Legal Medicine Organization of Iran (Tehran Autopsy Hall and Cemetery Offices) [1].
  • Personal belongings: Items found with the deceased are transferred to the police when family members are absent and are returned through the appointed carrier or released by the court once any investigation closes [1].

steps.title: Civil death registration and death certificates
steps.html:
• Registration with Sabte Ahval: Following medical certification of death, relatives must register the death with the National Organization for Civil Registration (Sabte Ahval) to obtain the official Persian death certificate (Gouahi Fout) and cancel the deceased's civil identity booklet (Shenasnameh) [1][2][9].
  • Abroad and consular tracking: If an Iranian citizen dies abroad or foreign relatives need Iranian civil updates recorded, families initiate registration and document authentication through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran (Consular Legalization and Mikhak System) or the applicable interests section [2][8].
  • Certified translations for overseas probate: Because Iran issues death certificates exclusively in Persian, any document needed outside Iran must be translated by an official certified translator and authenticated by the Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs [1].

steps.title: Local burial and international repatriation of remains
steps.html:
• Absence of cremation and commercial funeral directors: Iran has no commercial funeral directors and no cremation facilities; municipal cemeteries, local mosques, churches, or recognized religious communities coordinate domestic burials according to the deceased's faith [1].
  • No objection and exit clearances for repatriation: Families arranging international repatriation must engage an approved local transport carrier in Tehran together with an international funeral director, secure a diplomatic no-objection letter addressed to the Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, cancel any foreign residency visa with the Immigration Police, and clear the sealed casket through airport customs [1].
  • Passport cancellation: Where the deceased held a foreign passport, relatives should coordinate cancellation with the issuing country only after repatriation documentation is complete if the passport is required for exit clearance [1].

steps.title: Iranian Civil Code succession, probate courts, and inheritance tax clearance
steps.html:
• Mandatory Certificate of Inheritance: Civil death registration does not settle the estate; heirs must petition the competent Iranian court or designated judicial authority for a formal Certificate of Inheritance (Gouahi-ye Enhesar-e Verasat) before banks or registries allow asset transfers [1][2].
  • Islamic and minority personal-status succession rules: Under the Civil Code of the Islamic Republic of Iran (Articles 825 and 906 to 915), statutory inheritance follows mandatory Islamic shares unless an exception applies for recognized religious minorities; under Article 907 sons inherit twice the share of daughters, while under Article 913 a widow receives one-quarter without children or one-eighth with children (compared with one-half or one-quarter for a surviving husband), and wills cannot exceed one-third of the net estate without other heirs' consent [3][4].
  • Direct Taxation Act inheritance tax clearance: Under Chapter 4 (Articles 17 to 24) of Iran's Direct Taxation Act, heirs must obtain tax assessment and clearance from the Iranian National Tax Administration (Inheritance Tax Clearance Offices) before releasing Iranian bank deposits, real estate, or shares; deductible items include standard burial expenses and established debts (including unpaid spousal mahr), dependent heirs with certified disabilities under the Comprehensive Law on Disability Rights framework qualify for higher Article 20 tax-exempt thresholds, and statutory pensions, social insurance, and life insurance payouts enjoy tax exemptions under Article 24 [5][7].

steps.title: Social security benefits and non-Apostille consular legalization
steps.html:
• Social Security Organization benefits: Families of insured workers should file death-benefit, funeral-expense, and survivor-pension claims with the Social Security Organization of Iran (Tamin Ejtema'i) under the 1975 Social Security Law, presenting the official death certificate and heirship documents [6].
  • Non-Apostille status: According to the Hague Conference on Private International Law (HCCH) status table, Iran is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; an Apostille sticker is not recognized in either direction [10].
  • Mandatory consular legalization: Every Iranian death certificate, Gouahi-ye Enhesar-e Verasat, tax clearance, or foreign Power of Attorney (Vikalatnama) requires sequential consular legalization through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran (Consular Legalization and Mikhak System) and the relevant foreign ministry or accredited diplomatic mission [1][2][8][10].

contacts.name: National Organization for Civil Registration (Sabte Ahval)
contacts.note: Registers deaths in Iran, cancels Shenasnameh identity records, and issues official Persian death certificates (Gouahi Fout).

contacts.name: Legal Medicine Organization of Iran (Tehran Autopsy Hall and Cemetery Offices)
contacts.note: Central forensic authority in Tehran (Behesht Street and Behesht-e-Zahra) handling autopsies, embalming, and repatriation preparation.

contacts.name: Iranian National Tax Administration (Inheritance Tax Clearance Offices)
contacts.note: Assesses estate assets and deductions under Articles 17 to 24 of the Direct Taxation Act and issues tax clearance certificates required to unfreeze accounts.

contacts.name: Social Security Organization of Iran (Tamin Ejtema'i)
contacts.note: Administers funeral allowances, survivor pensions, and disability insurance entitlements under Iran's 1975 Social Security Law.

contacts.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran (Consular Legalization and Mikhak System)
contacts.note: Certifies Persian civil records and translations for overseas use and authenticates consular Powers of Attorney (Vikalatnama).
